sections.overview: Amphibian Species of the World recognizes Hyla molleri across the Iberian Peninsula and into southwestern France. Its separation from H. arborea has been debated because morphological and call evidence is inconclusive in some studies.
sections.identification: A dark stripe runs from the nostril, across the eye and down the flank; the toes have adhesive discs.
sections.habitat: It uses vegetated wetlands, stream margins, temporary ponds, lagoons and wet meadows.
sections.diet: Available records indicate that adults eat mainly ants, with beetles and spiders also recorded; tadpoles graze plant matter and periphyton.
sections.behavior: Adults are mainly crepuscular or nocturnal and spend much of the year among riparian vegetation rather than in water.
sections.reproduction: Breeding usually runs from March or April to May or June, with eggs attached to aquatic plants in stable, vegetated ponds.
sections.ecology: The continuous flank stripe distinguishes it from the related Mediterranean tree frog, H. meridionalis.
sections.conservation: The Spanish biodiversity inventory lists global Least Concern in 2022, while regional assessments and habitat reports differ.
